author: sonnet
label: climb-02-01
changes: Added what the nightly comparison writes (one result row per day) to the mode section, and said gates A and B read it.
Added a Handover between engines paragraph: the taking-over engine charges only periods with no ledger entry, covering shadow to both and rollbacks.
Defined billing period, one ledger row per customer and period, and the pending row that marks an unknown-outcome charge.
Added how an unknown charge is resolved via the provider idempotency key, with RollbackBlocked if the provider cannot say.
Stated that skipped events are those logged since new_only began and replay starts from the new_only clock.
Stated that workers check flag and rollback record before every charge, how in-flight charges are handled, and who opens the record (on-call or the charge monitor).
Defined gates reset concretely and named who writes the result rows, resolves mismatches and records sign-off.
Merged the duplicated gate reset wording in After any rollback; trimmed a few failure-table phrases.
Extended open question 4 with the failure definition; added open questions 8 (sign-off tooling) and 9 (mid-period switch).
Gate B row: the move to new_only sets the flag and the new_only clock together, and the old engine stops computing when it next reads the flag (Q15).
Handover rule now treats a ledger entry marked not charged as 'no live entry', so the old engine can charge it (Q12).
Added 'Who runs it' paragraph: on-call or monitor opens the rollback record, a worker runs the steps, on-call acts only in RollbackBlocked (Q9).
Stated that nobody charges between halt and catch-up and due periods wait for the catch-up (Q10).
new_only replay step now says where it writes (shadow store) and why it precedes the flag flip (Q11).
Replaced 'After any rollback' with 'Ending a rollback': who closes the record and that closing clears the gate counters (Q13).
Added open question 10 for an unconfirmable charge in RollbackBlocked, and linked it from the drain text (Q14).
Shadow store description now notes it also holds the old engine's recomputed invoices during a rollback.
Diagram: added RB_S --> RollbackBlocked on step failure.
Diagram and failure table: removed 'times out', replaced 'nears 35 day expiry' with 'replay not finished by day 35'.
Rollback steps: added 'Failures and restarts' paragraph (one open record at a time, crash counts as step failure, on-call resumes from saved step).
Rollback replay step: stated that the oldest skipped event expires on day 35.
Gates table: added what decommissioning does to the flag and old engine.
Where state lives: removed the oldest-skipped-event timestamp from the rollback record, since it equals the new_only clock.
Failure table: merged the step failure rows into one rule covering all rollbacks and worker crashes.
Open questions: added 11 (step time limit) and 12 (decommission shadow store retention).
Cut the Scope and assumptions section to one short paragraph
Merged the separate 'Handover between engines' and 'Double-charge and dropped-charge protection' sections into one 'Never charging twice' block with the unknown-outcome resolution
Merged 'Who runs it', 'Failures and restarts' and 'Ending a rollback' into a single Rollback section; removed repeated statements that periods due during rollback wait for the catch-up

Removed failure-table rows that duplicated the gates table or rollback section (charge rate trigger, rollback step fails, manual refusal, replay past day 35, gate not met detail), leaving a pointer note
Moved the mismatch-rate definition into the comparison paragraph and dropped it as an open question

Merged open questions about decommission details and mid-period switch into one item, folded day-35 boundary and in-flight rollback into one item, and renumbered; all open questions are together at the end
Shortened table wording and the state-lives bullets, removing repeated explanations of the record override
holes: Q3: Who or what measures the charge failure rate over a 10-minute window, and what does it count as a failure (declined cards, provider errors, timeouts)? What does the automatic trigger actually do to start the rollback? (author: The brief does not define a charge failure. I assumed provider errors and timeouts, not customer declines, and listed it in open question 4. A charge monitor counts new-engine charge attempts per 10-minute window and, above 2% failures, opens the rollback record, which halts new-engine charging; the rollback steps then run. Who owns the monitor is not decided.)

Q14: What does on-call actually do in RollbackBlocked for an unknown charge the provider can't confirm? How do they decide charged versus not charged? (author: Not known how on-call should decide charged vs not charged when the provider API cannot confirm. Plausible sources are the provider dashboard or the customer's bank records, but I have no verified procedure, and if still unclear the brief's two constraints (no double charge, no dropped charge) conflict. Added as open question 10 and pointed the drain text to it.)

Q16: How long can a rollback step run before it counts as timed out, and what does 'nears 35 day expiry' mean in days or hours? (author: The brief gives no step time limit, and I will not invent one. I removed 'times out' from the diagram and text, so a step fails only on an error or worker crash, and added open question 11 for the limit. 'Nears 35 day expiry' was vague, so I replaced it: the oldest skipped event is logged at the new_only clock, so it expires on day 35, and a replay not finished by then goes to RollbackBlocked.)
